text:
Had an old gtx 1080ti gpu and naturally was starting to show its age (the fact it lasted so long shows how great a gpu it was, and depending on use still is). I decided to upgrade. I was contemplating getting this or an AMD gpu. I got this because it's Nvidia and the driver support is much better than AMD. I have a PCIE 3.0 motherboard and this requires a PCIE 4.0 motherboard (PCIE is backward compatible so the latest gpu will even work on a PCIE 1.0 port). I decided to get this anyway as it's only 1 generation below and I am essentially loosing 5-10fps which is nothing massively different (essentially with each generation you will be loosing no more than 5-10fps, depending on the system it is added to; so each newer generaton would near enough double by this amount). I only need to upgrade the motherboard if it is 2 generations or more above, as than the performance is noticeable (much lower fps and slower texture pop-in and the like). I got the rtx 4060ti 16gb gpu (won't go anything lower with vram since 8gb should be the least of it nowadays and 11gb the standard due to how demanding applications are today).

Having got it, benchmarked it and tested it in various ways I can safely say it is a great card. I got it and benchmarked it natively (without dlss or any performance support) at maximum settings "by todays standards" getting near 24-30fps on the lowest and about 33-50fps on average (obviously anything older will be much higher). I take it if I had a PCIE 4.0 port I would get an extra 5-10fps. So anywhere from 29-55fps at maximum settings. This gpu can handle pretty much anything thrown at it and with the addition of adding frame generation an extra 30-40fps is gained on max settings. Also it's nice that this gpu is doing all this and using near half of what my 1080ti used in terms of power. Which saves some money with electricity bills. The one issue I have is the 128 bit bottleneck, which they should have made it at least 192 bits as performance would largely have been increased. But this is understandable as this would have used more power to do so. The gpu is incredibly efficient and does alot with what it has. It stays cool and quiet pretty much all the time even in demanding situations. Has "incredible" overclocking potential considering its only using 1 pcie x8 connector for power; this is very impressive but as said limited by the 128bit memory bandwidth. It is very efficient with what it has.

The gpu is really a 1-2k card, and can go 4k depending on the application used, though if incredibly demanding will require frame generation which adds so much fps it is unreal. Overall a great gpu, as if you are upgrading from a 1080ti like me a big leap in terms of performance but if you are coming from a 3080ti the leap is nothing major besides adding frame generation (unless you specifically want this feature; but will depend on application support). So anything below a 3080ti is worth an upgrade. Only 4x/5x nvidia gpu cards can do true frame generation because of an Optical Flow Accelerator and newer tensor cores (AMD has their version but is largely inferior due to lack of hardware support and being "mostly driver based"). As said adding frame generation provides so much of a performance boost it is unreal (anywhere from 30-40-fps). Overall a great card, though my only gripe is could be a little cheaper. That is the only issue with the gpu, they should have made it cheaper to reflect its performance (as in native performance without frame generation or dlss). Overall though, a great gpu.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Oh, where to start. First of all, my PC is a HP Pavilion p6110f, which this GC upgraded for me.
Introduction: The EVGA Graphics card is a good upgrade for those on a old Computer such as a 2009 based PC. It's easy to plug into a PC using PCI express, and works very well on any pc with that one thing. However, there are certain flaws a gamer and PC enthusiast should be aware of.

Design Choices: The Design of my model of the Graphics Card has a large heatsink. This makes it difficult and impossible for me to install another GT 730. Its fine in my honest opinion, but the idea of having a fan for less space makes me want to replace this card with that.

Hidden Costs: Oh yes, this has them. First of all, if you're upgrading a PC from the early 2000's, or anytime before PCI express, you have to upgrade the motherboard! Now, I had the luck to avoid that problem, for my motherboard has 1 PCI express x16 slot, but its a hidden cost for people who are using a old PC. Second hidden cost is Power. Most PC's have a 250 Power supply, which was sufficiant for my PC, but if you don't have 300watts, you're not pushing the Graphics card to it's limits. What I mean is, it does work with 250 watts, but for a gaming rig, it's not fully pushed to its potential. So, thats another hidden cost TO A GAMER.

My Experience: The Graphics card was easy to install, drivers breezed through. However, 2 months after I recieved this, (Yes, don't ask why I review it now) My HDMI port dies on me, making it impossible to have a TV/PC monitor combo, a small loss, but it sucks a bit for video editing.

Overall: The GT730 Graphics Card is a nice upgrade, but for gaming, I suggest a more expensive card, such as the 970 for gaming builds.

text:
Für die Auswahl dieser Karte, die nicht gerade die schnellste ist, waren 3 Kriterien maßgebend. Erstens sollte sie 2 DVI Ausgänge besitzen, zweitens steht nur 1 Slot Breite zur Verfügung und drittens sollte auch noch Windows XP unterstützt werden. Da ich sie nicht für Spiele sondern nur für "normale" Büroarbeit benötige, ist deren Leistung für mich zufriedenstellend.

Die darauf befindliche GPU GF108 ist noch in 40nm Technologie gefertigt und entspricht dem Stand von 2011. Die GT 730 wurde 2014 neu aufgelegt, ist aber leistungsschwächer als die GT 440 aus 2011. Der Unterschied liegt in der Taktrate, bzw. TDP. Die GT 440 hat eine TDP von 65W und die GT 730 eine von nur 49W, benötigt also weniger Kühlleistung. was sich positiv auf die Lebensdauer auswirkt.

Mehr als 4 Sterne kann ich ihr nicht geben, da sie nicht dem aktuellen Stand der Technik entspricht.

text:
Je suis très peu gamer. Les rares jeux auxquels je joue sont des titres déjà anciens (GR Wildlands, Red Alert 3, Elite Dangerous) et cette carte est déjà surdimensionnée pour ces titres. Mon avis ne concernera donc pas l'utilisation en gaming.

Si on oublie un peu le jeu, je voulais l'équivalent des performances d'une RTX A4000A (ex-série Quadro) pour mon utilisation dans une station de travail (i9 12900, 64gb DDR4, carte mère sans fioritures) sous Windows 10 Pro. C'est exactement ce que fait la 4060TI 16gb, avec une architecture Ada Lovelace récente. La GeForce est légèrement en dessous, de très peu et sur quelques points qui ne sont (dans mon cas) que des détails.

Le gros intérêt de cette carte est clairement une combinaison de performance (GPU Ada), de quantité de VRAM (16Gb), de sobriété énergétique (moins gourmande qu'une 4070TI mais un peu plus qu'une petite RTX A) et de prix encore abordable.

Cette carte n'est pas du tout idéale pour le gaming. Elle est trop chère pour une 4060TI à cause des 16gb de VRAM. Mais ce n'est pas son rôle, puisque c'est une carte pour les créateurs : modélisation 3D, rendu GPU et IA, traitement vidéo, etc. Dans cette optique, la 4060TI 16Gb est un bon plan.
Son orientation "pro" est compréhensible, compte tenu du fait que le constructeur qui la propose est PNY. C'est aussi PNY qui construit la quasi totalité des Quadro/A. Il y en a peut-être d'autres, mais toutes mes cartes Quadro venaient de PNY, depuis ma toute première Quadro FX1100 (ça remonte).

Très bonnes performances pour le prix (pour les créateurs professionnels sur CUDA/RT Cores), largement suffisante pour le jeu occasionnel sur des titres récents, inévitable pour les utilisateurs d'IA (CUDA & Tensor). C'est le ticket d'entrée pour la création avec des outils de dernière génération.

Excellent! Well worth the investment if you can afford it. The most important component of a pc. Everything else in your system relies on it, so why not protect them the best you can. The warranty is VERY long, so it could be used on multiple pc builds before you need to upgrade (as long they don't keep changing the GPU power cables. Figure it out NVIDIA!).

Seasonic really takes care of you with this PSU. The TX-1300 comes with all the current cables that you will need (including a 12v 2x6). And it comes with a nice PSU tester! I HIGHLY suggest using the tester first, before you get into hooking up any cables to the motherboard. You can even test the PSU without a motherboard. It could save yourself alot time trouble shooting. One GREAT bonus feature of the tester is that it is also a 90 degree adapter for the 24 pin cable. You can leave the tester on and use it permanently (I emailed Seasonic support to confirm). Helps with esthetics and better air flow.

Another feature is that it has auto fan mode if you want it quiet. I have not heard it once yet while gaming, so I leave it in standard mode.

-VERY SMALL cons:
It comes with clear wire combs that I found to difficult to get on to the individual wires. They were very tight, so the wires are difficult to put in. I had to had to stretch them with my teeth (I am not proud about this or recommend). I am still deciding if I like the clear plastic of the combs also. I think I prefer black or white better.

The TX-1300 is long. Make sure you have room in the case. I have the FLUX PRO, which has an option of installing a PSU sideways for better cable access. I was not able to use this feature of the case, due to the PSU length. No big deal.

All and all, this is a excellent PSU. If you want high quality 1300 watts, this is the one to get! No doubt!

text:
Bought it to replace an old Seasonic X Series XM2 1250w PSU that I bought in 2016, it started making weird noises from the fan and I thought it's time to buy an ATX 3 PSU and be future proof. This PSU is awesome and so silent, loaded it up to 1000w and the fan didn't even spin! The cables are easy to route and all of them are flat and sleeved. The title of this amazon listing is a bit misleading as it has 1300w in the title but you will receive the correct 1600w ATX 3.0 version. The title mentions 1300w because in some power outlets it will give you a max of 1300w (100-240vac (1300w) vs 115-240vac (1600w))

I wanted to get an ATX 3.1/PCIe 5.1 PSU but I read the differences are so trivial and only in the 12VHPWR plug (now called 12V-2x6 in the ATX 3.1 spec), what matters is that your GPU be ATX 3.1 with H++ marking on the power plug. The PSU plug doesn't matter whether it's 3.0 or 3.1 because it won't be moving and the cable will be fixed in place all the time. You also have to know that the 12VHPWR cable remains the exact same regardless ATX 3.1 or 3.0.
Also worth noting that he ATX 3.1 spec allows for a lower hold up time so it's worse in that regard.

Awesome egpu frame/enclosure. It allows you to customize your egpu how you want. Use whatever ATX PSU you want, the card you'd like, etc. It works great. I took a bit of a risk considering how few reviews there are, but im really happy with how it turned out. It works perfectly with my RTX 3080ti and be quiet! PSU. 10/10 would buy again. I recommend this to anyone looking for a versatile/customizable egpu that works great without breaking the bank.

The only other thing I'll mention is the little circuit switch on the board. In the instructions, it shows you what the switch looks like and says that it comes switched on as the default position, but mine seemed to be switched off. So, if your egpu doesnt start up at first, try turning it off, flicking that little switch, then turning it back on again. Worked perfectly for me after that.

(And, as always, make sure to plug your PSU into a good outlet! Preferably with some kind of grounding/surge protection)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
A few things:
-Currently using this EGPU with RX9060xt 16gb version PowerColor. The device is paired with an AsusVivobook S14 2024, it works like charm, plug and play, download adrenaline and the sofware will do everything. Once installed, Windows/Adrenaline will detect the external GPU and it will offer you the extra power, no regedit modifications neither reset, the internal graphics card wont bother the big one. People dont like to mention this, for EGPU build, AMD is perfect, plug and play.

-Using this will a Rog Ally X, as you may know, you have AMD drivers for the device and AMD drivers for the graphics card (they can crash each other). When you plug this it will take sometime to detect the card and it will install (without telling you) the drivers. I turned off the device, reset and the ROG Ally X showed me a blue screen. It will tell you a severe crash system occurred, you hit continue it will ask for a recovery serial number. GOOD NEWS is, you dont have to do all of it, just ignore, reset and bum. The device will turn on without issues.

After this event (and to avoid this), muy suggestion is before connecting this device, go to device manager, search for screen drivers, you will see the ROG ALLY AMD drivers and DISABLE IT. Screen will change the color profile and will be handled by Windows, no worries. Plug the graphics card and open adrenaline. The device itself will tell you that the adrenaline version from the ROG ALLY is old, it will install a new version with the drivers for the graphics card. After this, enable again the drivers and you are ok, both drivers wont bother each other. You plug the graphics card, it will detect as an external GPU and the device will handle everything. Make sure to use a good HDMI cable with the graphics cards (i have a really old one and wont display the signal, you will be worried about the device not working), but no, everythings is ok. This product works.

A few considerations.
-The usb 4 cables are short, this is something done on purpose. The shorter the cable, it can handle more power for the GPU, it will give you the full 40 gbps.
-Modern graphics cards sometimes WONT SPIN the fans. This is a modern feature when they will use it if the device is hot. If not, then the fans wont spin (dont think the device is not working. Use the USB4 cable, connect to your device and start gaming, they will work normally.

Hope this information helps, an amazing product. I will check for a differen USB 4 cable, maybe I can see a more powerfull one.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: You just spent hundreds, or possibly thousands, on a high-end graphics card. Now you must hide it between the other PCIe cards and the heat sinks around the CPU. Any RGB lighting or decorative finish on the graphics card is lost amid the other elements of the computer build. The natural solution is to use this Vertical Mount, which displays your graphics card so the intended fans, decorations, and RGB lighting are visible through the tempered glass side panel of most contemporary computer cases. In addition to the visual benefits, mounting the graphics card horizontally causes most cards to blow heated air from the radiator out the back, which means it exits right over the CPU socket. This is true whether you are using an air cooler or an AIO liquid-cooling method. With the card in a vertical position, the hot air has a chance to exit and be pulled out through a normal configuration of exit fans on the back side of the computer case. Finally, when your graphics card is mounted horizontally, the PCIe slot takes a lot of side-to-side pressure, especially with higher-powered cards due to their weight. Even adding an additional support, which has become a necessity, only alleviates this somewhat. A vertical mount is not an issue in that regard. In fact, it assures your card will remain in contact with the riser's PCIe slot, even with its weight alone. The conclusion is that a vertical mount has all the pluses and none of the negatives.

text:
Thunderbolt 3/4（USB4対応）のeGPUエンクロージャーです。
別途、ATX電源とGPUが必要です。
一般的なNVIDIA／AMDのPCIeグラフィックカードを搭載可能。85WのPD給電にも対応しています。

今回はかなり変態的な構成で検証しました。 
母艦は iMac (Retina 5K, 27-inch, 2017)（Radeon Pro 580搭載）。
さらにThunderbolt経由で、外付けNVMe SSDからBoot Camp環境のWindows 11を使用しています。

今回は、このiMac上の Windows11に、eGPUに GeForce RTX 3060 Ti を接続するという構成です。
そのままでは認識はするものの、コード 12: 「このデバイスが使用できる空きリソースが不足しています」が発生するため、以下のような対応を実施しました。

・OpenCore Legacy PatcherでMMIO領域を拡張
・Windows側でPCIメモリ空間を大容量確保 
・Display Driver Uninstallerで元々入れていたRadeon関連ドライバを完全削除＆使用停止 
・imac 上の Thunderbolt3のポートをeGPUのみ使用する、今まで動かしてきたWindows11用のSSDは暫定でUSB 3.1 ポートから起動するように変更

これらを行うことで、RTX3060Tiは コード12のエラーを回避することができ、正常に認識するところまで確認できました。
これだけでも正直かなり感動です。

ただ、FF15のベンチマークを実行したところ、スコアが思ったほど伸びず、内蔵のRadeon Pro 580を上回る結果にはなりませんでした。帯域や構成の影響が大きいのかもしれません。

さらにNVIDIAのドライバを最新版へ更新したところ、ブルースクリーンが発生。
環境依存の可能性が高いため、いったん検証は中断しています。
次は内蔵SSDに正規手順でBoot Campを構築して再検証する予定です。

肝心のエンクロージャー自体ですが、ハードウェアとしては接続すれば素直に認識します。
今回のような変態的な構成でなければ、一般的なThunderbolt対応PCではスムーズに使えるかと思います。
特殊な検証環境では工夫が必要ですが、製品そのものは堅実に動作します。
eGPUを検討している人、（ただしThunderbolt 3/4 USB4は必須）には、夢が広がるケースだと思います。

text:
まず、ハウジングについてですが、基盤が剥き出しなので扱いに少し困ります。
最近はグラボでも裏面にハウジングがあったりと、eGPUで使うことを考慮されているようなので、肝心のドックが基盤剥き出しなのは残念です。

Thunderbolt4(TB4)のみ対応で、OCulinkに対応していないのはやはり残念です。
最近流行りのミニPCではOCulinkが対応していることが多く、TB4よりもOCulinkの方が速度が出るためです。
そのため、PCIe16レーンもPCIe3.0(x4)となっています。（OCulinkだとPCIe4.0(x4)になることが多い）
ゲームなどには体感でそこまで影響は与えないでしょうが、動画処理などでは違いが出てくるかもしれないです。

背後（ポートが無い側）の12V電源ポートについてですが、「接続しているPCに電力供給するため」かと思いましたが、違いました。
こちらは、「ドックに電力入力する」ためのものです。
ACアダプターなどで動作するような軽量級のグラボしか使わない人には良いのかもしれませんが、そういう人はそもそもこのようなドックも必要が無いと思います。
また、メインのTBポートもPD85Wですので、ミニPCをPCのみで動作させるには少し心もとないです。（ノートPCなら問題ないでしょうが）

右側のTBポートは、15W給電で何に使うのかと思いましたが、TBデイジーチェーン用のポートのようです。
サンダーボルト4対応のドッキングステーションとか持っている人には便利かもしれませんが、私の利用用途では有効な利用法を思いつきませんでした。

この製品はノートPC利用者向けには☆4つ、ミニPC利用者向けには☆3つと感じました。
やはりOCulinkが欲しかったです。

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Updating my review:
After deep investigations under different linux distributives, it turned out my HP EliteBook 860 G11 considers it as a DMA threat, and rejects to properly initialize the eGPU. The system's hardware-level security (likely Sure Start, because DMA Protection had already been turned off) flags the external PCIe device as a DMA threat, leading to a critical resource allocation failure. While the system correctly identifies and reserves 16 GB of VRAM in the upper memory range, it stubbornly refuses to allocate the essential 64 MB of 'low memory' (Base Address Register / BAR 0-2) required for the initial handshake. As a result, the kernel fails to bridge the device, leaving the eGPU in a 'zombie' state where it's visible in the tree but completely unusable for rendering.

So, technically, it's unsupported by most business laptops.

Not working with 5060 Ti 16GB.

title: 2.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Cable did NOT work out of the box for Dell Poweredge R730.
From what I can tell, this cable ignores the sense functionality of the R730 riser in such a way that it's a luck of the draw whether the cable works. In my case, my GPU didn't receive power

In order to trigger the riser to power the GPU, there needs to be continuity on the following:

GPU Pin 1 -> Riser Pins 4 and 8
GPU Pin 4 -> Riser pin 6

My cable satisfied the first condition, but not the second. After I repinned it, my GPU works correctly.

ADDITIONALLY, the cable is not keyed in such a way to prevent plugging the cable in backwards, which could short 12v to ground. It's very important to make sure the riser side is connected to the riser and same to the GPU.

Functionality:
I was using this to hook a Nvidia Tesla P40 to a Dell Poweredge R730xd. I had just purchased the P40 and thought there was an issue with it. I was about to return it because the computer could see the card running: "root:~# lspci | grep -i nvidia 82:00.0 3D controller: NVIDIA Corporation GP102GL [Tesla P40] (rev a1)" but I found nothing running "root:~# nvidia-smi No devices were found" I tried multiple Nvidia drivers and tests with no luck. Finally I took a multimeter to the cable coming from the PCIe riser and found pin 6 that should have been 0v was reading -3.3v.

I Googled it and the solution was that it was a sense pin that had been wired to ground. I spent way too long getting the pins out using tweezers and staples and swapping pins 4 and 6. As soon as I plugged the cable in with the wires swapped, the card was recognized right away.

It took two days of troubleshooting to get this fixed. I should have started with the cable, but I was focused on the GPU and drivers.

text:
I usually don’t leave reviews, but I’m seriously upset and feel like I need to warn others. I bought this Thermaltake Toughpower GF A3 1200W thinking I was getting a top-tier PSU — fully ATX 3.0 and PCIe 5.0 ready, supposedly built to handle RTX 40 series GPUs. I followed everything to the letter. Used the included 12VHPWR cable, routed it carefully with zero bends or stress. I’ve built dozens of PCs — I know what I’m doing.

After less than a week of use, my system powered off randomly. I opened the case and was shocked to find the 12VHPWR connector partially melted, with visible scorching on both the PSU port and the cable. It was literally starting to burn inside my case. This is not just a defective unit — this is a fire hazard.

Thermaltake has no business marketing this PSU as compatible with high-end GPUs when this kind of thing is still happening in 2025. They know these issues exist with poor pin contact or internal defects and are still shipping these units out. And Amazon, you shouldn’t be selling something this dangerous without better QA.

If I hadn’t caught it early, this could have fried my entire PC, including my $2,000 RTX 4090 and possibly caused a fire. Absolutely unacceptable.

If you care about your hardware or your home, stay far away from this PSU. I wouldn’t use this again even if it was free. I’ll be switching to a brand that actually takes safety and quality seriously.

This is the worst purchase i've ever used.
